#4119. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#4118. Video: Sonic's 'Memories And Beyond' 35th Anniversary Animation Released

Can Sonic and friends defeat Metal Sonic?

Earlier this year, Sega announced a new Sonic the Hedgehog 35th anniversary animation short, titled ' Memories and Beyond'. Now, months on, it's been officially released.

It runs for around 13 minutes and has a story by Takashi Iizuka and written by Ian Flynn. It sees Sonic and friends try to stop Dr. Eggman from harnessing the power of the Chaos Emeralds to upgrade Metal Sonic into the "ultimate fighting machine".

This passion project has been in the making for the last 12 months, and is the fourth collab with GSX productions. It follows Sonic X Shadow Generations: Dark Beginnings, Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds: The Animation and Shinobi: The Art of Vengeance DLC Animated Trailer.

To celebrate the launch of this new animation, the Sega Shop is also releasing a special-edition 'Memories and Beyond' t-shirt, featuring artwork inspired by the animation. Metal Sonic will also be appearing in the upcoming Sonic the Hedgehog 4 live-action movie, arriving in cinemas next year.

#4117. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on modern platforms and with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

Bad signal or dead zones? Download your issues before you leave and read anywhere.

#4116. GTA 6 Gets 20 Seconds Of New Gameplay, And Everyone Can't Believe How Real It Looks

Here's a bit more footage that has also just appeared today:

Original Story: Sorry to keep bombarding you with GTA 6 hype, but we're literally one week away from the biggest video game launch of all time, and even 20 seconds' worth of gameplay is getting millions of views ahead of November 19th's launch.

This latest footage comes from a weird source - an Instagram account called "Only in Dade". The gameplay shows someone cruising down the road and looking at supercars out the window, while a mass of NPCs are also shown either admiring the vehicles or just making their way down the street.

Here's the footage (we can't embed the original, so you'll find the Reddit repost below):

This is clearly a marketing stunt and not necessarily representative of what you'll be seeing in the game, but it does appear to be real GTA 6 footage - Rockstar Games was spotted sharing and liking the video shortly after it went live.

It also appears to be a take on a similar real-life video from Miami that was taken last month:

Our best look at gameplay for GTA 6 to date has still been the Extended Preview from back in August, which certainly gives us a better idea of what to expect than 20 seconds' worth of gameplay.

We'll take anything we can get at this point though, and it's making the wait even harder for November 19th!

You're probably aware by now of the scandal at Nvidia. Outgoing CEO Jensen Huang has announced his departure following allegations of two extramarital affairs within the last week. This is reverberating through the tech and games industries, causing Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney to weigh in.

He did so on Twitter, where he expressed considerable respect for Huang. "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity," he writes. "Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction."

In the interest of my own sanity, I'm going to gloss over anyone calling the transition of CEOs anywhere a "sad day for humanity." Nonetheless, Sweeney continued tweeting about the matter.

A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction.November 12, 2026

"It’s terribly sad and, in my opinion, far too much government heavy-handedness - including through leaks and anonymous sourcing to journalists with dubious motives - no excuse for abandoning due process," he says, presumably in reference to the reporting and current internal investigations going on surrounding the alleged impropriety.

The government involvement stems from the belief one of Huang's relationships was with a potential Chinese operative. Information is limited at present, and is likely to remain so for the foreseeable future.

"Look at all of the free passes government has given to Apple in its efforts to monopolize app distribution and payments - including cover for lawbreaking here and in allied nations overseas," Sweeney adds in another follow-up tweet. "Selective enforcement and opaque dealing are antithetical to a free nation."

His first post referenced a tweet he made in 2024, celebrating Huang's position at the forefront of Nvidia and highlighting how closely Epic and the hardware manufacturer have worked in the past, particularly through the Unreal Engine. How that business agreement continues is something that'll need to be worked out with Huang's successor.

#4114. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4111. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

Here's how you get to all three Sha-Chi Towers and Primal Stones for A Severed Mindseal in Phantom Blade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Completing the Phantom Blade Zero A Severed Mindseal quest takes a long time as you've got to help the friendly Mandate Shadow Warden at three Sha-Chi Towers scattered across the game. The Weeping Creek Valley tower is part of the main story but the other two are optional: the Pangzhen Tower, which is confusingly actually in Meigu Lake, and the Crimson Forest Tower, which can't be accessed unless you've sufficiently progressed the main quest and a particular side quest – in short, if you've just started this quest, you don't need to worry about the other towers for ages.Specifically, you've got to find a Primal Stone for the warden to chow down on at each tower, which involves unique exploration efforts for each one. So, to make this quest as simple for you as possible, I've explained every step of A Severed Mindseal below, including how to get to each Sha-Chi Tower and find all the Primal Stones.

The Primal Stone is on the first floor of the tower around the back of the central furnace, but you need the Sha-Chi Furnace Inspection Crank to collect it:

To reach the Friendly Shadow Warden at the top of the Pangzhen/Meigu Lake Sha-Chi Tower, you need to run along the Pangzhen docks in the northeast of the city. Keep going along the wooden jetties until the walkway structure starts climbing up the cliff. Follow it all the way to the top and you'll get to a rope bridge and the Pangzhen Sha-Chi Tower Upper Level 1 Bell. This leads to the tower's south entrance and the start of your ascent.

However, the Primal Stone is in the lower section of the tower, which can only be reached by boat. Get the Sha-Chi-powered boat from the Pangzhen docks and sail around to the north side of the tower. Follow the red lanterns and you'll end up going down a channel that leads to the lower portion of the tower, then proceed as follows:

You can't reach this Sha-Chi Tower until you've reached the Mirage Estate in Pangzhen and have found all three Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet Memory Flowers within to trigger the next step of the Phantom Blade Zero Triple Threat quest. Only then can you fast travel to the now frozen Mirrorwood area of the forest where the Sha-Chi Tower is:

There unfortunately aren't any specific rewards for completing this quest, but now that you have the tower key, you can unlock that door near the lift and plunder the rest of the tower. When you get to the roof, you'll bump into some familiar faces and can take on the Phantom Blade Zero Heart of the Fist quest and get a few crucial Soul Tempering materials for some of great weapons.And this also isn't the last you'll see of Spectral Blade. I won't spoil what happens but, now that you've completed his quest, you'll find him in Soulrend Cliff where he will also give you a Soul Tempering material for a weapon. Just beyond where you find him is also where you can wrap up the Phantom Blade Zero Cui quest.© GamesRadar+. Not to be reproduced without permission.

#4108. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4107. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

#4106. "The Series Was In Dire Straits" - Kit & Krysta Recall Zelda's Pre-BOTW Dark Times

While many of us can now look back on the Skyward Swords of the Zelda series with fondness, those who were in the trenches at the time might recall that things were starting to feel stagnant.

The later games of the 'traditional' Zelda formula were well received critically, but the tried-and-tested gameplay wasn't working wonders for their sales numbers, and they were struggling to bring in new fans in the process.

Cue the open-world series reinvention in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

With Ocarina of Time back in the public eye (perhaps the most typical 'Zelda' a Zelda game can get), there are some who are wondering why it has been so long since we've seen the traditional format. So, naturally, former Nintendo employees Kit & Krysta are on hand to remind us all just how dark things were getting before the invigorating shot of BOTW.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately about how the Zelda team 'ripped these [traditional format games] away from us at the peak of their popularity'," Kit Ellis said on the latest episode of the duo's podcast before setting the record straight.

"The series was in, like, dire straits," Krysta Yang added, "it was selling like nothing". Kit recalls going to focus groups and receiving feedback like, "the fanbase is dwindling; this is not bringing in new players; the interest is getting smaller".

With the huge success of Zelda today, it's easy to forget that such a time ever existed — particularly for those who weren't all that deep on the series at the time.

"It was depressing," Krysta adds, "it was like, we are losing this."

Of course, Breath of the Wild was so immensely popular and so very unlike anything we had seen from the series before that it gave Zelda the interest boost it so desperately needed. It's interesting to see how well-received the return of the classic format has been with OoT, so perhaps we'll see something slightly more traditional make an appearance in the next mainline game.

The dream scenario would be Nintendo leaving room for both formats to develop, but it's far too early to know what the team is cooking up for the next mainline entry. Until then, we have the pinnacle of the open-world structure and the very best of the traditional at our fingertips on Switch 2, so we're more than happy to wait and see what comes next.

Skyward Sword was also put into a weird position, I feel.

It required WiiMotion+ controls, and while they did work fine for me personally, for a lot of people it was really janky. And the failed tech demo of the game on stage where wireless interference made it almost impossible for them to show off gameplay really really soured a lot of gaming journalists and had a lot of people going in with a negative expectation. I remember article after article talking about how bad it would be. IIRC this was the last time Nintendo did their game announcements live - it's all been prerecorded Directs ever since!

Like I said, I feel it was largely fine. But it also meant the game couldn't be played as easily sitting down, and also meant that if you got the game without already owning a Wii Motion+ controller, you had to either get a new controller, or the adapter. (or get the game with the bundled controller)

The other aspect is that it was one of Nintendo's last (or was it THE last) games for the Wii - the push was being made for moving to the WiiU and the game didn't see any kind of upgrade for the WiiU other than it running through backwards compatibility. But there was no upscaled version or high res version or anything, so it looked like a Wii game on the new 1080p console.

That and the WiiU itself was a flop, and that didn't help either.

So I feel Skyward Sword just got super unlucky. And yes, it was rather linear compared to even Twilight Princess. But the story was really good but I wonder how much of it was the classic formula, or rather that it got mired in sometimes wonky controls, the pre-soured expectations, and being at the end of the Wii's life and not really getting a second chance until the Switch re-release. And even the re-release has it's issues - then Joy-con motion controls are not as reliably precise as the the Wii Motion+ controls and the pro controllers really show the game was not designed for classic controls at all.

@JohnnyMind I think you’ve hit the nail on the head with the sales data. Gaming as a whole was starting to recede in the late Wii era and we all knew the WiiU was a bomb. It was such a different landscape for gaming too.

That era’s “mainstream gaming” and today’s are very different. Gaming was still very much a niche hobby of sorts back then. A popular niche hobby, but still niche nonetheless. We were in the beginning of the live service transformation of the industry where most gamers wanted CoD or Halo and open world games were taking over and Nintendo, by contrast, was still delivering traditional style games.

I can totally see why Nintendo might’ve been nervous about what to do and how to adapt to how the market had shifted.

We forget too that, for all the success of the Wii and the DS, Nintendo hadn’t had the consistent domination they’re enjoying today, as the GameCube trailed far behind the competition. The Wii resuscitated them briefly for the casual market and most “serious gamers” were associating with PlayStation and Xbox at the time too.

The brilliance of their pivot with the Switch, BotW catering to the more “serious” gamers, embracing the indie market, and Mario Odyssey being a defiant and confident celebration of all things Nintendo is certainly a lesson for how to regain a crown.

"These two former Nintendo employees know absolutely nothing about Nintendo! I, the consumer, know the truth!" - A lot of you guys for some reason.

In June 2011, Ocarina 3D came out and sold pretty well. The it had given the 3DS another boom in units sold, but it didn’t last the whole Summer, resulting in a dramatic price drop for the system a couple months in, to make it cheaper than even the price which the DSi launched at.

But were certainly articles at the time about how Skyward Sword selling 3 million copies after the holidays was not satisfying enough. Both Donkey Kong Country Returns and Super Mario Galaxy 2 sold more than twice that amount. In the 2011 holiday season, Mario Kart Wii and New Super Mario Bros. Wii sold more, despite releasing in 2008 and 2011 respectively.

There was still certainly more hype and excitement than most games on the market. The big thing it was competing up against however was Skyrim, that just had universal praise and a virality like no other game at that time.

But, it was also a pretty late Wii game. Nintendo focused their efforts onto 3DS, which had made Skyward Sword a bit of a 2011 straggler. In that year, both Xbox and Playstation gained ground as incredible games were releasing then, alongside some more advanced motion-sensing technology to draw noise. The Wii was older news and had Skyward Sword released in 2010, like it was originally supposed to, I think you get a much different conversation about the popularity of that game. But, this sort of competition of Zelda getting slightly snubbed happens regularly too. Baldur’s Gate 3 narrowly sold more than Tears of the Kingdom, and snatched more awards too.

Regardless, in the 2013 Wii U Direct, Nintendo made it a point to say that the the next Zelda title after Skyward Sword would have its linear structure entirely challenged and go back to basics.

Before we even knew Breath of the Wild’s title, story, or aesthetic, Nintendo wanted to tell us that the structure would change and make it their selling point. You really only make that remark when you sense from your fans that they are ready for a change.

So, I do think that was because the series was viewed at as something very conservative in its approach and Nintendo caught on to that. The formula of a Zelda game was well understood and Skyward Sword did little to change that. Comparatively, A Link Between Worlds was looked at as something with a middleground between fresh and historied, being the sequel to the the game that would establish the “Zelda formula.” I don’t think it was in “dire straights,” to the extent that it was threatened as not being one of Nintendo’s most important franchises, but it was considered to be predicatable in its approach, and maybe even a little tired.

Skyward Sword was released in late 2011 when, as much as I love the console, the Wii was largely irrelevant. Twilight Princess was only 4 years old at that point and was a big hit as a launch title (TP is arguably the most ‘typical Zelda’ title there is, as it was designed to placate the backlash to the toon style of Windwaker and is very much a spiritual sequel to OOT and the Spaceworld 2000 demo we all expected would be the GameCube’s Zelda). It’s a bit disingenuous to suggest Skyward Sword sold badly due to being a ‘typical Zelda’ when really it was because most Wiis were probably gathering dust by then.

The Wii U we all know was a disaster, so again, blaming the low sales of Wind Waker HD and Twilight Princess HD on their typicality is not really accurate. BOTW was a Wii U title until (wisely) it was reserved for a launch game for Switch and a swan song for us Wii U owners. Had it not been a Switch game then there is no way it would have been the juggernaut that it turned out to be, with an install base of only 13 million Wii U owners.

A Link Between Worlds, OOT 3D and Majora’s Mask 3D all were good sellers on 3DS in the time between Skyward Sword and BOTW. In fact, the least popular Zelda game, Triforce Heroes, was the most different of all games and the time and was pretty much a disaster!

#4105. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4104. Resident Evil Requiem Wins GOTY As Xbox Takes Home Two Awards At The Golden Joysticks 2026

Wednesday night was a celebration of all the best games from the past 12 months, with the Golden Joystick Awards taking place in London's Troxy venue.

What a night it was for Capcom, as not only did they come away with Ultimate GOTY, and Console GOTY for Resident Evil Requiem, but the developer won another five awards including Studio of the Year.

In terms of Xbox's own studios, it's a familiar story to last year's Joysticks with Minecraft taking home the "Still Playing" award for consoles and PC, and Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations claiming "Best Game Expansion".

Altogether, there were 12 games all vying for the Golden Joysticks' most covenanted Ultimate Game of the Year award. Xbox's Forza Horizon 6 was in the running but it was a Resident Evil kinda night.

#4102. Review: CRKD Ult Pro Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - A Decent Pad Let Down By Awful Shoulder & Bumper Buttons

CRKD is the latest accessory manufacturer to produce a premium alternative to Nintendo’s own Pro Controller on Switch 2, but it’s one that needs a lot of refinement if it’s to become a legitimate competitor.

Priced at $69.99 / €79.99 / £64.99, the Ult Pro sits below the Pro Controller and roughly at par with Gulikit’s excellent TT line, price-wise. It comes feature-packed with TMR (Tunnel Magnetoresistance) analogue sticks, Hall Effect triggers, four back buttons, two extra bumper inputs, four profile modes, adjustable rumble, a charging stand, and more.

The analogue sticks feel good, featuring a more convex shape that you don’t often see these days. There’s a thin ridge near the edge of the grip which helps keep you aware of where your thumbs are sitting. It’s also worth mentioning that the grips can be removed for replacement designs, but these are sold separately – it would have been nice if at least one alternative were included in the box as standard. Otherwise, the TMR technology should keep stick-drift at bay.

The default D-pad design (again, you can swap it out if you want) is circular with a raised cross representing the four cardinal directions. I like this a lot: it feels quiet yet retains accuracy during gameplay, and I found it reliable for platformers like Super Mario World and action games like Contra.

The ABXY buttons unfortunately aren’t mechanical with a satisfying click, but they do the job well enough. Like the analogue sticks, they’re slightly convex in design and are spaced at just the right distance to allow easy, intuitive access to all of them. I also like the colours; CRKD avoided the exact same colour scheme as both the SNES and Xbox 360 pads, but it’s got the same vibe (you can also opt for an all-black controller, if you wish).

The shoulder and bumper buttons, sadly, let the side down. You can adjust the shoulder button travel distance, opting between a short, clicky input or a full, smooth trigger input. To be clear, the Switch 2 doesn’t support analogue triggers for anything except the Nintendo Switch Online GameCube pad, so your choice here is purely down to personal preference.

While the full-motion trigger feels pretty good, the clicky, tactile option is horrible. Rather than offering a satisfying click, they instead feel weak and spongy, almost as if the slightest bit of force will snap (or ‘CRK’, amirite) whatever mechanism is inside to produce the clicky response. I hated this, and CRKD should address it promptly for any future revisions.

As for the bumper inputs, the additional ‘L2’ and ‘R2’ inputs are far too close to the main ‘L1’ and ‘R1’ buttons on either side. So essentially, when resting your index finger across the bumpers, you’re covering both the standard button and the extra input, making it far too easy to accidentally press the wrong button. CRKD would have been wise to space these further apart and make the main bumpers larger (8BitDo’s Pro 3 is a good reference point), or just remove the extra inputs entirely.

Speaking of extra inputs, the four additional buttons on the rear are perfectly fine – I’ve got no major issues with these, and they’ll no doubt prove useful for anyone looking to gain the upper hand in Modern Warfare 4 (or perhaps even sprint while moving the camera in Ocarina of Time). The only downside is that they produce quite a loud click when pressed, though I think this is down to the plastic used for the exterior casing – it feels a tad cheap for the price.

You can map any input to the additional buttons — the four on the back and the two on top — by using the ‘P’ (Program) button underneath the D-pad. You also have four profiles if you want to swap between configurations. CRKD neglected to include decent instructions with the product, and the QR code for an online manual led me to a dead page, but it does at least have a video on YouTube if you need help remapping buttons and setting up profiles.

With the function buttons (i.e. Start, Select, Capture), CRKD bizarrely opted for two rocking inputs. With the left one, for example, you push it up for Select and down for Capture. It’s so weird – it works, but it’s weird. There’s no dedicated ‘C’ button; instead, there's an integrated macro to navigate to the Chat app if you push down on the right rocker.

You can connect the Ult Pro to your console via three different methods. Bluetooth is standard and works exactly how you’d expect: just hold down the large, black button until it flashes blue to enter pairing mode. You also have a USB dongle stored inside the charging dock, so plug this into your Switch 2 dock and you can pair that way instead. Finally, you can simply connect it via a USB-A to USB-C cable. The difference between these is, for me at least, not noticeable, but if you’re someone who’s particularly sensitive to lag, you might have a clear preference here.

Oh, and there’s no wake-up support for Switch 2. Sorry.

Finally, the Ult Pro lasts for around 15 hours on a single charge, and if you use the included charging dock, you’ll likely never need to worry about it dying on you. The dock design is simple and looks neat next to the TV when charging. You can also replace the rechargeable battery in the controller itself if need be, or simply use a pair of AA batteries.

There’s a lot to like about the Ult Pro, including its TMR sticks, the D-pad, the charging dock, and the lovely coloured ABXY inputs. Unfortunately, CRKD really dropped the ball with the shoulder and bumper buttons – I hate them, and they really ruin the whole thing for me.

With no wake-up support and a fairly cheap-feeling exterior case, this isn’t quite the Pro Controller competitor I was hoping for, but with some tweaks and refinements, I think the company could be onto something. Do I actually like those rocking function buttons, though? Honestly, I’m still not sure.

The sample used in this review was provided by CRKD.

#4101. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#4100. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

With the galaxy far, far away turning a half-century old next year, Hasbro is going back to basics with its Star Wars 50th Anniversary action figures; the Black Series, Vintage Collection, and Retro lines are all getting toys based on A New Hope.

Well over a dozen products are listed in this initial wave of Star Wars 50th Anniversary action figures, and they're all based on characters from the original movie that kicked everything off - from major names like Luke and Leia to Cantina wolfman Arleil Schous. They're all slated to arrive at some point in early 2027. While the Black Series and Vintage Collection Star Wars 50th Anniversary action figures are available to pre-order now at Hasbro Pulse and other retailers like Amazon, the Retro toys are exclusive to Target.

Regardless of the range, all of these toys are opting for "legacy-inspired packaging" to provide the ultimate throwback feel. You can get a better look at them below.

Adam Biehl, head of Disney action brands at Hasbro, noted that "for decades, Hasbro has been proud to partner with the STAR WARS brand to bring its unforgettable characters and stories to fans through play and collecting. The 50th anniversary is an extraordinary milestone, and it presents a tremendous opportunity to unveil a new wave of products that honors the legacy of STAR WARS while giving fans new ways to celebrate the saga."

This version of our hero is in the middle of the Death Star escape, so he's wearing a Stormtrooper belt and is wielding a grappling hook. The figure also comes with a blaster. Like all Black Series figures, this one is six inches and features multiple points of articulation for more convincing poses.

This version of Leia is so screen-accurate it took me aback. It comes with two blaster accessories and a hood, and comes in a 50th Anniversary black and gold packet modelled after old-school action figures.

This version of R2-D2 from the sands of Tatooine is a bit battered, but as is evident from the picture of his many accessories, he's ready to throw hands with anyone who'll get in his way.

A new, 50th Anniversary Stormtrooper snuck through the net of initial announcements and has been added to the lineup. It comes with a blaster accessory, ready to take the fight to the Rebels.

I have a suspicion this one's going to be very popular. Depicting Han Solo, Chewbacca, Leia, and Luke mid-escape on the Death Star (hence the Stormtrooper belts), they're incredibly convincing likenesses. They feature blasters and a grappling hook. Much like all Vintage Collection figures, they're 3.75 inches tall (with the exception of Chewie, who is presumably bigger).

The Dark Lord of the Sith is back again with a new Vintage Collection figure, and of course he comes with a lightsaber. You can have it ignited or just as a hilt.

Aren't you a little short to be a Stormtrooper? The classic baddie is ready to report, with blaster either in hand or holstered.

Remember this guy? The wolfman appeared as a background character in the Mos Eisley Cantina.

A surprise figure that wasn't in the initial 50th Anniversary announcement has joined the fray! New Hope R2 has been given the Vintage Collection treatment, and while he doesn't have any accessories, you can lower the central tread to show him trundling along.

It wouldn't be A New Hope collection without farmboy Luke, and this one features the signature (and incorrect) yellow retractable lightsaber seen in the original Kenner toys.

This toy recreates Han as he was in the Kenner days, with a hand nonchalantly resting on his belt. He comes with his trusty blaster too.

Kenner toys are infamous for their somewhat awkward robes, and that's been recreated here - though Leia comes out of it better than Obi-Wan or Darth Vader. She also arrives with a blaster.

The lovable Wookie is back in a nostalgic design, but by looking at his eyes I'm gonna guess this guy has seen things. He has a chunky blaster accessory rather than his bowcaster in its traditional form.

Darth looks really snuggly in that sleeveless trenchcoat. Don't tell him that though, or he'll smack you with his retractable lightsaber.

This old-school version of Obi-Wan has robes that wrap around him like a sleeping bag, recreating how those old Kenner figures would look. The lightsaber is extendable, but locked to the toy's hand.

Featuring R2-D2, C-3PO, and a Death Squad Commander, this is inspired by an early bird certificate package from Kenner (a placeholder box with cardboard backdrop) back in 1978.

This pack is an ode to the opening of A New Hope, where Stormtroopers shoot their way through Rebels on the Tantive IV. Both come with blasters.

This double-pack includes a couple of strange denizens from Tatooine, with a blaster for the Jawa and a gaffi stick for the Tusken.

It's all kicking off ahead of the saga's birthday with plenty of announcements. Although the new 50th anniversary Lego Star Wars sets are great, but I’m most interested in their weird collectible minifigures.

#4098. Asha Sharma Issues Statement On Xbox's 25th Anniversary And The Future Of Gaming

"Our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games"

We've been waiting all week for Xbox to acknowledge its 25th anniversary in a formal fashion, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has now issued a statement discussing the past, present and future of the brand to celebrate its birthday.

It's a pretty lengthy statement, and a lot of it is just about recapping the history of Xbox and Microsoft Gaming as a whole. Sharma talks about how things have come a long way since "Microsoft Adventure" in 1979, and then how Xbox was "impossible to miss" in 2001 while also revolutionising online play and being there for the launch of Halo.

There's also a cool high-definition ad for the original Xbox console that you can see down below.

"When the original XBOX launched in 2001, it was impossible to miss. It was 2-3x larger than rival consoles, with a giant X molded into a black enclosure and a bright alien green jewel at the center..."

"A year later, Xbox Live revolutionized online play with persistent friend lists and matchmaking, as well as a common service for developers to build connected experiences. And bringing all of this together was Halo: Combat Evolved, a launch title that not only defined XBOX but proved its first advertising campaign: “Games Will Never Be The Same.”

After going through the history, Sharma mentions that each of the 111 people who have worked at Xbox since the beginning will be getting "a special engraved console to commemorate what you’ve helped build".

She then references the fans, Xbox FanFest and how today's FanFest event in Seattle will "bring the celebration home".

"The story of XBOX has never been ours alone. Our fans have challenged us, cheered us on, held us accountable, and stuck with us. We’ve been celebrating this anniversary with fans around the world and special launches. Today, we are bringing the celebration home to Seattle."

And finally, the most notable bit in this statement is probably what she says about the "next 25" years of Xbox, highlighting that the "cost, resources, and risk required" to create modern games has grown dramatically, and that it's had an impact on the ability to turn ideas into games, or at least allow those ideas to reach their potential.

As a result, she says it's something that "must" be changed, and that people and small teams will "soon" be able to achieve things that currently require much larger teams and financial resources in today's world.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this."

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

There's some interesting stuff in here for sure, and we reckon it might be worth keeping an eye on tonight's Seattle Xbox FanFest event for any potential announcements - after all, it's the final stop and "home" destination for the FanFest tour.

For now though, let us know what you think about Asha Sharma's statement down below!

Yes, it shouldn't matter if a game is generated via AI if it's good and fun. But if anyone can generate a game for cheap, how will a game studio justify a large development team?

We're not there yet, but an industry which is aiming to reduce costs and increase profits will get us there.

Yes. The passage is strongly AI-related, although it never explicitly mentions artificial intelligence.

It appears to be alluding to the transformative potential of AI, particularly generative AI, in video game development.

1. "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

2. "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers."

3. "The cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown dramatically."

No. The passage deliberately avoids mentioning AI, machine learning, or generative AI.

The underlying message is that AI and emerging technology will fundamentally change the economics and scale of video game development.

The author is suggesting that the next generation of games will be created with fewer people, fewer resources, and significantly greater creative ambition.

The wording is particularly interesting because it frames AI not simply as a way to cut jobs or costs, but as a way to enable creative possibilities that were previously impossible.

My verdict: I would interpret this as an indirect statement about the future of AI in gaming, with AI likely being a major part of the vision, even though the passage carefully avoids naming it directly.

I'm probably in the minority here, @HonestHick, but I really do not care if a game is made entirely by AI (which it surely will at some point!).

The way I look at it is that AI is just a natural progression of the technological revolution. Just as with the Industrial Revolution, humans will adapt to it happening, and will find other means of employment, and just as with the Industrial Revolution it won't happen all at once, it will be a gradual process of replacing certain tasks within game development, with the dynamic of who does what changing over many years rather than all of a sudden. In a decade, when AI involvement will be much greater, it will be largely accepted that this is the way games get made. Right now, there is resistance within the gaming community, but as time goes on, and AI usage becomes more prevalent, so too will the acceptance of the gaming community that this is the way of things.

I think what will sway things is that games will be made faster; potentially a lot faster. AAA games that take 5 to 7 years to make now, will be made in 2 to 3 years, and then possibly fewer than that as AI improves and is more deeply implemented.

What should also happen, is that games will cost a lot less to be made, and hopefully that will be passed on to the consumer. If a game costs £200 million to be made now, it needs to be sold at £70 in the hope of recouping that money. With AI heavily involved, that development costs far, far less, and I think those companies that pass on those savings to the gaming community may find that it is very much appreciated.

So, if games can be made more quickly, and cost less, then I personally do not see the downsides of that because regardless of AI humans will always be involved somewhere along the process...

AI for testing would greatly help some studios, e.g., Bethesda, which reminds me that games like Starfield utilize AI to generate some of the planets through procedural generation.

I feel like the Oblivion remaster used AI. That is pure slop and still hasn't been fixed on consoles. But of course they had time to release it on Switch 2.

If AI can make games better than sure use it but don't produce lazy slop like we see on the stores these days.

Given the level that AIs are reaching, people had better get ready—this is the future of gaming, and there’s no point in complaining about it. Finally, developers are starting to speak openly about using AI in their games and studios. Enough with the nonsense; AI is the breakthrough the gaming world needs to cut down on development times, which keep growing with every new generation. Costs have also become increasingly absurd, driven by developers' salaries and the sheer number of people involved in each project. People claim they don’t want AI, yet they’re the first to complain when a game takes too long to develop—or when it’s released in a broken state.

@Fiendish-Beaver On this one, our mindset is far too narrow and your view of things is overly simplistic.

First of all, nobody was talking specifically about AI. AI is only one part of the tools that are available today to make game development easier. For years now, development tools and resources have become increasingly accessible to small teams and even to solo developers. Just remember Bright Memory, released in 2019 and developed by a single person using Unreal Engine. Back then, AI wasn't even being discussed the way it is today. Several of these tools are free, including Unreal Engine, and if you're passionate enough, you can develop a game on your own or with a small team without needing a massive budget.

As for AI, yes, of course it speeds up production processes. But that's not a bad thing. In fact, it's mostly a positive when you actually understand the topic. It can also significantly reduce production costs without sacrificing quality when used properly. I use AI every day, and it really depends on how you use it. You can accelerate production while remaining highly creative. It all comes down to what tasks you delegate to AI, how you use it, and what you keep as a human-driven creative process, especially when it comes to artistic decisions.

I don't think it's possible today to create a AAA game entirely with AI. Even Asha Sharma said so in a recent speech, particularly regarding the importance of creativity. If you're being honest, you should have acknowledged that. In any case, that's very different from the statement made by PlayStation's CEO, who openly said he wants to use AI to enhance creativity. We've also all seen the leaked demo of Aloy, the Horizon character, being generated and animated using AI.

So your point of view is extremely limited. AI is only one factor among many, and that factor can only help reduce production costs in the long run, lower game prices for consumers, and even free up more time for humans to focus on creativity when used correctly.

What she's saying is simply common sense about how the industry is evolving. That's all.

Also, I never said that Sharma was talking about AI, I said I read that and took from it that she was referring to AI. There is a difference. There is an inference in what she said, which you can read into as meaning AI, which is what I, and if you read through all the comments, many of us believe she was getting at.

I'm not sure whether you and I agree on what she said today, but I do think that she is hinting at AI being a big part of what is to come, or if not hinting, she is leaving it unsaid but expecting us to realise that is what she is talking about.

When it comes to what Sharma said a few weeks back, she and I are in agreement, because she and I both said that they are not able to make AAA games using AI right now. That's right now. In a decade or so, who knows, it may well be possible (that's assuming AI has not enabled the creation of a bio-weapon that wipes us all out first, of course!).

Anyway, I'm not sure what I said that is 'extremely limited' because I said that AI will make making games faster and cheaper. It is a tool, and it will be used as such, and like all tools throughout the history of man, they are used to make our lives easier. Quite how that statement is extremely limited, I'm not sure...

@HonestHick My man of reason. Keep it going!

@Fiendish-Beaver Sorry, I stopped after your first two comments, which implied she was only talking about AI and suggested it wasn't a good thing. I read your other comments afterward and saw that you became more nuanced following other people's replies.

Either way, I still maintain that she was talking about the evolution of the industry in general, the accessibility of development tools, and how easy they are to use for small teams—hence my example of Bright Memory, which was created by a single person in 2019 and without AI (generative AI didn't even exist yet).

Of course she's also implying the use of AI, that goes without saying. Who doesn't see AI taking an even bigger role in video games? It's obvious!

And we agree: when used properly, AI is ultimately a good thing for the consumer (maybe a bit less so for developers handling low-value tasks)—it all depends on how it's used.

Sorry if I misunderstood you, but next time please try to be less divisive and more nuanced in your initial comments, because I admit I don't always read the entire thread

@Fiendish-Beaver You are not the only one to think this - it is quite clearly what she is saying - she's just being carefully to not state her vision is AI. We knew this from the moment she was appointed, so there is little suprise. I'm of the same mindset, @Titntin. I won't boycott a good game using AI just because it uses AI. All I really want, at the end of the day, is to enjoy the games I play, and if it is created using AI so be it.

I don't want to sound heartless, and I don't like the idea of passionate developers using their jobs, but throughout history man has developed tools to make their jobs easier, less laborious, faster and ultimately cheaper. People losing their jobs to a new technology has happened ever since the start of the Industrial Revolution began.

Worldwide, as new tools and methods became available, we saw miners replaced by machinery. The same happened in the car industry where robots replaced human workers. In each of those examples (which happened in my lifetime) the workers found alternative employment, and the same will be true of game development; as AI becomes more and more capable, it will become more and more prevalent, and as it does more and more developers will find themselves being replaced (which I think is what Sharma is banking on as she dismisses 3200 employees this year). Many of those developers will move to other studios not yet in a position to deploy AI and still needing the human guiding hand, and some will move to completely different employment.

Ultimately, I think human involvement in gaming will always be a thing, but over the next decade, many of them will be gradually replaced, and we, the gamer, will embrace the good games that come out. If AI is not up to the required standard, then the games will fail, but as time goes on, I can foresee that many of the games we play will have had heavy input from AI, and providing they are good, we will simply play what we are offered, and our protestations regarding the use of AI will gradually peter out just as happened with all the strikes when the car industry was changing, for example, and we will accept that change is inevitable because like it or not change is coming...

#4097. Zelda: A Link Between Worlds Listed As 'Playable With NSO', But Let's Not Jump To Conclusions

Nintendo's official website for the Zelda series has updated its entry for A Link Between Worlds with a mysterious 'Playable with Nintendo Switch Online' icon, leading some to believe that it's a hint of an upcoming expansion to the paid service. However, we're not so sure.

The site is home to a series timeline, listing every mainline game from the NES original through to the Ocarina of Time remake. The likes of A Link to the Past, Link's Awakening and Oracle of Seasons are all marked with a 'Playable on NSO' button and, indeed, you can play all of them on the service. A Link Between Worlds has been locked to the 3DS since its launch back in 2013, however. Not only is it decidedly not playable on Nintendo Switch Online, but there isn't even a library for the console.

However, there are just as many replies that seem to take a similarly cautious approach to us. You see, the button is missing on Oracle of Ages — a game that notably is on the NSO library — and none of the series' other DS games have any sign that they're playable, too. Hmm.

We're chalking this one up to a simple mistake, then — we wouldn't be surprised to see the message removed soon enough. There have been rumblings of a dual-screen addition to the NSO library ever since we first learnt about the Switch 2's bonus USB-C port (remember those mock-ups for an extra screen add-on?), but it feels very unlikely we'd find out like this.

Ah well, back to our 3DS copies we go, then...
