Do you think this button is a sign of things to come or a simple mistake? Let us know in the comments.

With a Democratic midterm win, a mini AI crash in China, and Jensen Huang admitted to an affair this Sunday, Nvidia was already in a tight spot. Now, a second affair allegation has come out about Nvidia's CEO, and the AI company's share price has taken a hit as a result.

This reported second affair is said to be with another Nvidia exec, Kimberly Powell, and now the GPU company turned AI company is investigating whether or not it should oust the long-time CEO.

Naturally, that instability is worrisome to some investors, who appear to be signalling distrust towards the company in light of these scandals.

To put the stock dip into perspective, at close on Friday, Nvidia stock was worth $188.70 a share, a dip from a high of $239.24 on October 6. This morning, after-hours trading puts it at $161.88, as of the time of writing. We haven't seen a share price as low as this for Nvidia since well over a year ago, at the end of June 2025.

With this after-hours trading figure in mind, Nvidia's market cap (share price multiplied by outstanding shares) works out to around $3.93 trillion, which is just under half a trillion less than its market cap before the affair with Alice Huang came out (between $4.3 and $ 4.5 trillion).

Accounting for a share price of $173.73 at close yesterday, that would make a $300 billion dip overnight (from $4.2 to 3.9 trillion). Naturally, one can't assume that downward trajectory will continue to decline, but if Huang is in fact let go, Nvidia shares could see a further drop.

This doesn't mean Nvidia will be closing its doors tomorrow. In fact, it's still a hugely valuable company that remains a market leader in the AI hardware arms race. If you want a top-of-the-line AI chip, you're going to Nvidia before anyone else. And AI has proven to be excessively valuable over the last few years, turning Nvidia into the most valuable company in the world at one point (though Apple has since surpassed it).

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Still, as the Nvidia board ruminates on whether or not to get rid of arguably its figurehead at this point, it's unclear where the company goes next and what it will do to regain that value. My bet is more and more AI and sadly not more affordable gaming GPUs. Sorry, people.

#4095. Xbox Playback Is Now Available, Take A Look Back At Your Xbox History

"Your games. Your milestones. Your story."

One of my favourite things to do is look back at the Xbox games I've been playing, the achievements I've unlocked, and all of my cool unique stats that make me the Xbox gamer I am.

This year, Xbox is doing something a bit different. Unlike previous Xbox 'Year in Review' roundups, which cover the past 11 or 12 months, Xbox Playback takes things all the way back to the beginning, celebrating your story through Xbox's 25 years.

You can access your own Xbox Playback from the official Xbox site, where you'll need to sign in with your Microsoft account. There's this whole song-and-dance animation, sorta like Spotify's Wrapped, which takes you through stuff like the first game you played, what year you played the most, what % of most played time across all of Xbox, achievements, and loads of other really cool stuff. Then, you can share it to social media if you fancy.

As you can see above, Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet created his account in 2006, has earned 28,528 gamerscore, and has 4,375 hours played: which is only in the top 4.8% of hours played, whereas yours truly is in the 0.2%. What can I say? I guess I'm an Xbox gamer after all.

Another thing that's really cool about Xbox Playback is that, for the first time ever, players will be able to access and view it directly from their console. No browser required. According to Xbox, it should appear soon, so keep an eye out!

We're keen to find out what your Xbox Playback says about your journey with Xbox through the years, so please do let us know what that looks like down in the comments. What percentage of hours played are you? What was your first game? When did you join? Let us hear it!

#4094. 'Genital Exposure Has Never Appeared This Frequently': GTA 6 Was Almost Refused Release in South Korea

GTA 6 was, reportedly, very close to being refused classification in South Korea just a couple of months back. The reason? Too many penises.

According to Inven's findings, the country's ratings board — the GCRB — was completely split on its initial classification vote. Three committee members voted for an 'Adults Only' rating, and another three voted to have Rockstar's game refused outright.

The report claims that the "frequent background appearance of male genital nudity without any sexual context" was the big sticking point.

In other words, there are a lot of instances in GTA 6 where male genitalia is on full display — even when there's no sexual context attached. The ratings board found this to be "excessive" in comparison to other games where genitalia may appear.

"It is not that genital exposure is completely forbidden, but it has never appeared this frequently without context," reads one of the committee member's statements.

It continues: "I do not believe genital exposure to this extent falls within acceptable limits under the current [ratings] standard."

However, the opposition's argument attempts to bring context into the equation: "In this game, scenes with heavy exposure are not particularly sexual. Conversely, in sexual scenes, exposure is limited. We must judge the content holistically."

In the end, following multiple postponements and even some regulation adjustments, a second vote was cast and GTA 6 was handed an 'Adults Only' rating. This time around, only one member voted for refusal, and eight pushed for Adults Only — so the argument for the latter was clearly quite convincing.

Apparently, a fear of simply missing out on GTA 6 also factored into the decision. There was an unwanted "pressure" in being the only country to potentially ban the game from sale.

Adding a bit of extra spice to this story, Korean outlet Gameple is now reporting that South Korea may be the only East Asian country where GTA 6 is not censored in some form.

There's evidence to suggest that Japan's version will be "modified" in order to adhere to region's often strict classification regulations.

Meanwhile, in mainland China, it's looking likely that GTA 6 won't be eligible for government approval, due to the crime-filled, violent, and sexual nature of its content.

What do you make of all this? How would you feel if a game like GTA 6 actually was banned from sale in your country? Keep your pants on in the comments section below.

#4093. Mini Review: Sonic Pico Park (Switch) - Charming Puzzle-Platformer Returns With A Nostalgic Co-Op Collab

Pico Park is a fascinating success story for developer Shunsuke Miyake, who created the original game over a decade ago while working at Sega. A cute, minimalist and deceptively challenging puzzler, it exploded in popularity with the introduction of online co-op and a feature-packed sequel that was released on Switch in 2024.

This new spin-off takes the escalating challenge of multiple puzzle modes and invites Sonic and his ever-expanding menagerie of friends to the party. Available on both Switch 1 and 2, Sonic Pico Park takes the core mechanics of Pico Park and adds a suite of design features from the Blue Blur's 16-bit heyday.

Challenges range from effortless, like walking forward and pressing a button, to lateral conundrums involving spikes and insta-kill barriers. Other mechanics offer slightly taxing fun, especially anything that requires the party to be tethered together. Then there are the absolutely punishing experiences that will have you yelling at each other or laughing your heads off (sometimes both).

Three distinct modes offer a balanced spread of co-operative and adversarial challenges. World Mode separates 15 distinct puzzle scenarios into four stages of increasing difficulty. Battle pits teams against each other to collect the most rings. Endless has you run a gauntlet, trying to last the longest without making a mistake.

All of this is livened up by the inclusion of Sonic and pals, with some nicely presented nostalgia to help ring (pun intended) in his 35th anniversary. All of the series' characters are selectable, with a couple specifically tuned for large-character puzzles, like Big the Cat. The series' iconic rings form the basis of Battle mode while also adding an extra mechanic to certain puzzles that require precise calculation of invincibility frames. Elsewhere, there's a pinball minigame and a top-down version of the Sonic 2 bonus stage.

It's a great game to play on the go, although you will need others, because there is no solo play available. Its bright colours and visually sparse stages are complemented by simple controls well suited to the Joy-Con. There's also something deeply satisfying about hearing those classic Sega sound effects coming out of the undocked speakers.

Sonic Pico Park is a good little game for multiple players to have fun with, and it more than caters for Sonic fans looking for yet another nostalgia fix.

Resident Evil Requiem walked away with the biggest prize of the night at the Golden Joystick Awards yesterday, capping off a total of four wins with the prestigious title of Ultimate Game of the Year. But in an acceptance speech delivered on-stage by Leon Kennedy actor Nick Apostoledes, there was an allusion to an even bigger winner - Capcom itself.

"What can I say?" Apostoledes began. "Resident Evil going 30 years strong this year - how fitting is it to win Ultimate Game of the Year for Requiem? We are just honored to be part of a project that is so beloved, a franchise that is so beloved. Thank you to the fans, thank you for keeping this alive. Capcom, you cannot fail."

Apostoledes' remarks were followed up by pre-recorded comments from Requiem director Koshi Nakanishi, who said he was "thrilled" to accept the award, and spoke about how encouraging it was for a single-player game to win, especially in such a crowded field.

While Resi itself will be making the big headlines, however, Apostoledes touched on an interesting point: the legendary run that Capcom itself is on. As well as claiming two GOTY titles for Requiem, that title also secured wins in the Best Game Trailer category, and a Best Lead Performer win for Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano. But two of Capcom's other titles - Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword - were also in contention for several categories, each one claiming its own win. Onimusha took the prize for Best Audio Design, while Diana actress Grace Saif took home Best Supporting Performer for her role in Pragmata. With three out of its four major releases this year claiming wins, perhaps it was of little surprise that Capcom would also take home the prize for Studio of the Year.

2026 has been a jewel in a crown that Capcom has been polishing for some time now. In the last four years, it's been on an excellent run. The last time a new release has slipped below a MetaCritic score of 80 was 2023's Exoprimal, and the closest thing it's had to a flop was Monster Hunter Wilds, which was plagued by performance issues. Elsewhere, it's been turning Resident Evil back into an essential release, breathing new life into classics, and successfully bringing life to new IP. It's been a relatively slow, quiet process, but Capcom has rarely put a foot wrong since 2020, and the community is starting to take note. 2027 looks like a quieter year for the studio, but with Resident Evil Veronica on the horizon, it looks like fans will still be eating pretty well.

#4091. Hang On, Firefight Is Coming To Halo: Campaign Evolved

Halo: Campaign Evolved isn't dead, people!

Firefight has just been announced as a free update for Halo: Campaign Evolved, arriving sometime this winter. The series' staple co-op PvE mode is locked in, with more details set to be shared at Halo Fest on December 12-13.

Halo: Campaign Evolved received some backlash for its lack of multiplayer options, particularly PvP and Firefight. I thought the criticism was understandable, but perhaps a little unfair given the game was always marketed as a campaign remake.

"For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies. The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update.

We’re kicking things off tonight at XBOX FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across new maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds."

Forgive my opening sentiment, but I honestly wasn't expecting anything new to come from Halo Studios. Especially after the developer was essentially reduced to a skeleton team, with future Halo production being handed over to Activision.

I'm a huge fan of Halo: Campaign Evolved, and whilst I'm still sad the teased Halo 2 remake seems unlikely, you should have seen me leap out of my seat when I spotted the announcement that Firefight was on its way. Hoorah!

If you add additional modes and features later they need to feel additive not pulled from the day 1 version. Too often Xbox feels like the later, releasing games that feel incomplete at launch.

#4090. AMD, Sony Mark PS5's 100 Million Unit Milestone with Signed Consoles

PS5 is the fourth Sony system to officially ship over 100 million units during its lifespan, and it may be the manufacturer’s most impressive achievement yet.

The firm has nimbly navigated a global pandemic, semi-conductor shortages, US electronics tariffs, a slumping global economy, and now AI-induced price increases to achieve the feat.

It remains within touching distance of the PS4 life-to-date, despite the latter costing less than half the PS5’s price at the same point in its lifecycle.

Celebrations are in order, then, and current PlayStation CEO Hideaki Nishino caught up with AMD’s Jack Huynh to sign some consoles fresh out of the factory.

AMD is obviously a longtime partner of Sony, and is currently working extremely closely with system architect Mark Cerny on bespoke solutions for the PS6.

Even amid the current component cost crisis, it’s going to be fascinating to see what the two companies concoct. PlayStation hardware typically punches well above its weight thanks to smart optimisation and great product design.

I know the sentiment around Sony is wildly negative right now, but I do think some degree of credit has to be given to the company here.

While it’s far from perfect, I think the PS5 is a little underrated by enthusiasts, as it’s delivered a remarkable roster of software with very good performance across the board.

I’d put this generation’s woes more on business decisions and poor communication, as opposed to the actual product.

#4089. Nintendo's On The Hunt For A Digital Archivist To Preserve Its Rich History

With closing online storefronts, the move to digital media and the rise of streaming, there are few gaming industry topics more discussed right now than preservation. Fortunately, it looks like Nintendo is making an effort to ensure that its history doesn't get lost to time (thanks, Time Extension).

Nintendo of America is currently hiring a Digital Archivist to "support the preservation, organization, and accessibility of historical hardware and software information," according to the job description. In short, this person would be responsible for ensuring that all things Nintendo are kept safely stored away and easily accessible.

We're sure that there are a few of you lovely lot reading whose brains are already like a Nintendo archive, and it certainly sounds like the job comes with its fair share of perks. The chosen applicant will surely have unrivalled access to Nintendo's historical records, get the chance to "Interview subject matter experts and long-tenured employees to capture institutional knowledge," and organise one of the richest histories in gaming. Damn, and there we were getting a kick out of putting our important paperwork into colour-coded binders.

What's extra cool is that this will be the person responsible for finding and dishing out these records to anyone at Nintendo for future use — you know, for when someone comes asking who that moustachioed fella in the denim overalls is.

Of course, the job comes with a huge amount of technicalities, too. The listing requires "Experience developing metadata structures, taxonomies, classification systems, or naming conventions," is looking for someone familiar with "metadata and archival standards such as Dublin Core, DACS, EAD, PREMIS, MODS, or similar frameworks," and has at least two years of previous work in Records, Metadata, Knowledge, or Digital asset management. In short, it isn't for any old Joe.

But hey, what an opportunity! This is a 12-month contract based out of Redmond, WA, and it will presumably result in Nintendo's 100+ year history living on for many more to come.

If you think this one might be for you, you'll find even more about the job in the official listing.

Feature The Nintendo Museum Goes Hard On Merch & Fun, But Could Dive Deeper Into History

What do you make of this job listing? Let us know in the comments.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It was bad enough for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that he admitted to having an affair with someone, who people believe to be someone suspected of being a Chinese spy. But it's now come to light he has reportedly had a second affair with a member of Nvidia staff—Kimberly Powell, VP of healthcare. After this latest story it's looking more likely that Huang could be forced to resign.

The question is what's next for Nvidia if the board today decides his tenure as the longest-serving Silicon Valley CEO should come to an end. Huang has been the image of the company in the eyes of the public for a long time, so whoever steps in to replace him will have a big leather jacket to fill. And whoever it is, it will be a major change for the company regardless.

The doors are wide open for Nvidia in the long-term, so it's difficult to pin down with any certainty who any eventual replacement CEO would be, but in the interim the options are more limited. Here's who we could consider seeing as the new CEO of Nvidia.

The first thing to note is that if Huang does get the boot, Nvidia will need to appoint someone to the position quickly as an interim CEO. As one of the biggest companies in the world and a major player in the AI industry which is keeping large parts of the US economy afloat, trying to quickly mitigate economic concerns will be key. This would likely mean picking someone internal to Nvidia.

Top of the list here is Nvidia CFO Colette Kress. If you've listened to Nvidia earnings calls, you'll have heard Kress talking to investors about how the company's doing. Kress could be a likely pick for interim CEO because she's known to investors and heads up company finances. In the short term, to investors she'd seem a safe bet to keep the company in good financial standing amidst any damage Huang's controversies may have done to Nvidia's long-term future.

Other options internal to Nvidia aren't out of the question, either. Jeff Fisher is especially noteworthy because he's very public-facing, but he is very much couched in the world of gaming as SVP of the GeForce department. Kress would still likely be a safer bet for investors.

Chief technology officer, Michael Kagan, is another option, and would potentially be a good fit as co-interim CEO alongside Kress. Kagan joined Nvidia as part of the Mellanox acquisition, a company which he co-founded. He is also a former Intel engineer having managed the design of the Pentium MMX chips.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The other Nvidia staff I listed are an option, too. Malachowsky perhaps not so much—he's a co-founder but is very hands-off and maybe doesn't have much real involvement with the company from a leadership position.

Any interim CEO that's picked could be there for a while. When Intel CEO Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018—under vaguely similar circumstances to those Huang finds himself under now—both he and Pat Gelsinger were followed by interim CEOs for months before final decisions were made on their successors. Though in Krzanich's case, the interim successor, Robert Swan, went on to become full CEO for another two years.

In the long-term, the net for Huang's replacement could be cast far and wide. People like Tim Cook and Elon Musk would be pretty outside bets, but with the monopolistic and 'in-bed-together' state of Big Tech in the US, it wouldn't be out of the question. Remember that Nvidia is the biggest profiteer of the AI boom by far, so an offer would be enticing.

AMD's Lisa Su would be an interesting choice, too, and has been touted by a number of people. She certainly has a combination of GPU and AI engineering prowess alongside general public trust and goodwill. In fact, I can't think of many tech CEOs that the public hate less (an increasingly relevant metric, these days).

Then there is also the consideration of who would want to take the job. Sure, it would guarantee a big pay check, but it's a big role to fill with Nvidia's current very flat hierarchy, and any CEO is going to have to be across everything the company does. It's also a role under intense political and economic scrutiny and with the potential for an AI pop still on the horizon, the company might be sitting on a precipice.

Of course, the board of directors could throw us a wild card, and on that front your guess is as good as mine. Though one thing is very likely, whoever comes in is probably not going to have PC gaming much in their thoughts.

3. Best mid-range: Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB

Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born. Since then, Jacob's led a double-life as part-hardware geek, part-philosophy nerd, first working as a Hardware Writer for PCGamesN in 2020, then working towards a PhD in Philosophy for a few years while freelancing on the side for sites such as TechRadar, Pocket-lint, and yours truly, PC Gamer. Eventually, he gave up the ruthless mercenary life to join the world's #1 PC Gaming site full-time. It's definitely not an ego thing, he assures us.

#4087. Three Special Football Jerseys Go On Sale To Celebrate Halo's 25th Anniversary

I've always had a thing for video game edition sports tees. They're breathable, durable, a bit weighted, and usually feature something subtle from a game I like on the front.

Xbox and sportswear company Dyenamik have already teamed up in recent weeks with to ship a range of gorgeous Xbox 25th Anniversary shirts. Now they're back with a new collection of Halo Anniversary tees, and they're looking very tempting.

The Halo shirts seem to be on available now if you fancy popping one in your sports bag. Individually, they'll set you back £70, with worldwide shipping available. Alternatively, you can grab all three in a Limited Edition Anniversary collection box for £175. Just be mindful that only 200 boxes were made, so you'll want to be quick!

So, let's go through them - here's a look at all three:

The legend himself. A black jersey carrying a grey halftone print of the Master Chief's helmet, scaled up across the back and wrapping around the front, with crisp white piping, a white HALO wordmark and the Master Chief's helmet just below the collar on the back.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

A tribute to the olive green MJOLNIR armour that made Spartan-117 the face of Halo. Black side panels, a black hexagonal pattern cascading across the shoulders and fading down the back, and chevron-striped cuffs, with 117 running down the left sleeve and the Master Chief's helmet and the UNSC eagle on the chest.

The AI who guided the Chief across the first Halo ring. The jersey fades from bright cyan to deep navy like her holographic form, with fine horizontal lines running through it like streams of data. White piping, Cortana's data chip and the UNSC eagle finish the front, with the Halo ring emblem just below the collar on the back.

A premium branded box finished in silver foil, with space to store and display all three jerseys together, kept the way a Spartan keeps their kit. Only 200 boxes are available, made for the fans who have been finishing the fight since 2001, and this collection is the only way to get one.

What do you think? Initially, I thought the black one was my favourite, but the blue Cortana jersey is growing on me. It is ultra vibrant and a perfect tone of blue.

£70 is no joke for a shirt, but it seems to be par for the course when it comes to sportswear these days. The Xbox 25th Anniversary collection is bleddy lush too, so worth checking those out whilst you're at it!

One version of the GTA 6 map has apparently leaked. The low-detail map doesn't reveal the full network of roads and areas in the game, but it does give us early confirmation of some in-game locations and a general outline of Leonida's highway system.

As for the likely real map, it names GTA 6 locations across Leonida, from Little Cuba on the outskirts of Vice City to Pelican Valley far to the south. #4085. Romancing SaGa 3's Great Looking PS5 Remake Moves Its Release Date Away from Persona 4 Revival

Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United will no longer launch just two days before the relative juggernaut that is Persona 4 Revival.

Previously set to release on the 16th February, the promising JRPG remake has actually been moved forward. It now drops nearly two weeks earlier, on the 4th February.

Square Enix must have read our coverage of the initial announcement, where I suggested that its release date was a real problem!

It'll almost certainly benefit from the increased breathing room — there's just no way it can compete with Revival's Xbox-partnered marketing heft — but it's still launching during a very busy period for new games.

The hope, then, is that Destinies United can stand tall on the basis of its quality. The original Romancing SaGa 3 was ahead of its time in terms of player choice and gameplay freedom, offering up an adventure that's split between a sizeable roster of protagonists.

Your actions determine the story's direction — and the fate of its characters — with the remake promising a particularly grand retelling thanks to its fully 3D visuals.

The remake also features a reworked turn-based battle system, difficulty settings, and a freshly arranged soundtrack. It certainly doesn't have the budget of Persona 4's, er, revival, but it's still packed with classic JRPG potential.

Are you waiting on Romancing SaGa 3's remake? Are you glad that its release date has been moved? Make your choice in the comments section below.

Woah, woah, woah! As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, it's been announced that 21 original Xbox games are coming to PC via backwards compatibility today, joining the four that were made available earlier in the year.

If you already own any of these games for your Xbox console, you'll also now get a PC version for free, and each title apparently also supports mouse and keyboard in addition to a traditional controller.

"We’ve also improved performance and stability for the first four games and every game now supports mouse and keyboard too."

It's also worth noting that four original Xbox games have added support for achievements today, with those being the two Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic titles along with Blinx: The Time Sweeper and Conker: Live and Reloaded.

Microsoft says that more original Xbox games are coming to PC backwards compatibility in the future, and achievements will be added to other OG Xbox titles as well.

What a great surprise for the 25th anniversary! I can't wait to play Star Wars and TimeSplitters on my ROG Xbox Ally X.

Users of Humble Bundle—the pay-what-you-want game-bundle storefront that will also sell you books and software—have been alarmed by a new redesign that seems to have axed a foundational piece of login security tech.

The just-released new Humble Bundle website has no support for two-factor authentication whatsoever: users are unable to add it to their accounts, while those who had previously set it up on the old site design (including yours truly) are able to log in with just an email and password. At no point in the login process does the site ask you to input a 2FA code.

Humble Bundle does not address the removal of 2FA anywhere on its new site. In fact, the site's FAQs still feature articles encouraging users to make use of it to keep their accounts secure, which is currently impossible. I have reached out to Humble Bundle to ask if the change was intentional and if it will be reversed, and will update this piece if I hear back.

This is, to put it mildly, concerning. The point of two-factor (or multi-factor) authentication is to make user accounts—which, on Humble Bundle, may well have credit card info saved to them—more secure. Even in the event your account password became compromised, your attacker would be unable to get into your account without also having access to your 2FA codes, which are constantly regenerated and only valid for short periods of time. In a world where too many people have bad password hygiene, it's a vital bit of security tech.

Unsurprisingly, Humble Bundle users are aghast at the uncommunicated weakening of their account security. "This is insanely bad, they need to take down password changes entirely until this is fixed", wrote one user in the Humble Bundle subreddit. "I can't even see a way to remove saved payment details anymore, this is seriously dangerous and the site should be taken offline until fixed ASAP", wrote another. They all, uh, they all pretty much go like that. No one is happy about this.

I have to imagine this was not an intentional change. Indeed, I can't fathom the circumstances under which it would be intentional. Either way, while 2FA's absence endures, you might want to play it safe and remove any saved payment details you have tied to your account, though some users report having trouble doing that, too.

#4082. These New GTA 6 Clips Look So Real, Fans Can't Believe It's All In-Game Footage

Another GTA 6 video has gone live from onlyindade, and it too has a strikingly realistic look.

Here it is, with the clip focusing on several vehicles in a police escort:

The signpost in the upper left features in-game locations, confirming that this is also in-game capture — though it's definitely aiming to ape reality.

Here's a direct comparison with real life:

Original Story: If you're at all interested in GTA 6, you'll probably have seen this doing the rounds already. A video is going viral on social media, because it's fooling people into thinking it's real-life footage — but it's actually the game.

Originally posted by onlyindade on Instagram, the video has since been shared by the official Rockstar Games account, with many taking that as confirmation it's actually a video of Vice City within GTA 6.

The clip begins with a view from inside a moving vehicle as it drives past the Cortez Hotel, a Vice City location inspired by the real world Colony Hotel in Miami. The view flips half-way through, looking out onto the road.

We see several custom cars (the same ones that have been recreated in real life) as well as an impressive number of NPCs going about their business.

It's extremely convincing; the way the camera sways mimics the sort of videos captured on smartphones. You can actually see a direct comparison of the video against real life here:

Fans are getting really excited about this new clip as it really highlights the game's attention to detail and realism, with some still unconvinced it's actually GTA 6.

#4081. You can make a vampire hunter who's afraid of the dark, disease and small spaces in Hunter: The Reckoning - Deathwish, and that's surely the best way to play

A month or two back I penned a 1500 word whine about feeling too powerful in Blood of Dawnwalker. "Gimme a vampire sim in which I'm a pathetic vein-nibbling goblin," I wrote, using many more adjectives than that. Well, never let it be said that I'm biased against vampires, for I am equally keen to play an RPG in which I am the least capable vampire hunter in the universe. A vampire hunter who screams when he wakes up with his hair over his face. A vampire hunter who has to spray the vampires with antibac before staking them.

An RPG like Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish, perhaps, which presents you with a choice of Advantages and Flaws when creating a character. You have to balance these out on a gnarly weighing scale, before they'll let you through the game's front door. Here is a video showing all that off, together with a lot of sixpacks.

The Advantage/Flaw system looks familiar on the surface. Advantages include Warrior, which gives you +15% chance of a critical hit, or Charmer, which gives you a +1 to Persuasion skill checks. Flaws include clumsy, bad reputation, fear of darkness, hypochondriac, and claustrophobia.

I don't know much about the tabletop game on which Deathwish is based, and the video skims the detail here, but I suspect the last three Flaws will boil down to something like "-1 Constitution in Unlit Closets". Still, I really enjoy the idiocy of going up against crypt-dwelling undead while being unable to tolerate shadows, small spaces, and disease. In general, I'd love it if Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish steered well away from any possibility of simply overpowering the vamps, to say nothing of the werewolves and other creatures of the night.

This appears to be the idea: devs Teyon have stressed their desire to make something more story and investigation-driven, after the stomping gibfest that was RoboCop: Rogue City. As narrative designer Mateusz Działowski put it in a previous dev diary, they've "switched from action with RPG elements into RPG with action elements". Amongst other things, you'll need to put together a team of fellow would-be slayers, each with secrets and traumas, and gather clues about best tactics while roaming the game's condensed and shiny New York City. You can read more about it all on Steam.

Some Marvel fans are hopeful that Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman will make an appearance in Avengers: Doomsday after the pair has been given an "additional writing credit" on the film.

The official WGA (Writers Guild of America) entry for the film lists the writing credits as follows: "Stephen McFeely and Michael Waldron and Eric Pearson and Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers and Jeff Loveness and Andrew Lanham and Destin Daniel Cretton and Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman."

It's Marvel... so anyone could pop up at quite literally any moment in time. I mean, just look at that surprise post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest. Elizabeth Olsen told press more than once that she would not be appearing in Avengers: Doomsday on account of the whole her being dead at the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness... but she's indeed back in action, albeit under the control of Doctor Doom, in the upcoming movie.

Because the inclusion of pre-Disney Fox-owned Marvel characters in Deadpool and Wolverine led to the inclusion of the pre-Disney Fox-owned X-Men in Doomsday... it would make a whole lot of sense for Deadpool and Wolverine to appear, especially since the oncoming incursions that are set to destroy several different universes... not just the MCU's Earth-616. We'll just have to wait and see.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18. For more, check out our guides to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#4079. itch.io will soon let you filter games with genAI disclosures out of your search results on the site, after admitting it was previously "critically lacking"

itch.io has unfortunately, much like Steam, long had an issue with genAI content being uploaded in droves, drowning out perfectly good games made by human hands. The apparent standard method against this, voluntary genAI disclosure, has been itch's primary tool to combat this wave of low-quality slop, but hasn't worked out too well; itch revealed a few days ago that 'the number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past two months'. Now, in attempts to further combat this, beyond just game assets requiring a genAI disclosure to upload as they have for two years, itch will be expanding the mandatory disclosure to tabletop games, books, comics, and soundtracks, as well as adding a 'no AI' filter directly into the search function.

itch noted in this announcement that its previous moderation of genAI use in projects had been "critically lacking", presumably referring to the unfathomable exponential increase in games being uploaded in the past few months by people who don't give a fuck about creating anything themselves and happily contribute to the death of the planet. itch went on to post "Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop" which, I mean, sure, cool! And, look, as many, many people in itch's replies have pointed out, this is not the same as outright banning AI.

Unfortunately, my question at that point becomes: how? itch is not Steam, not a storefront backed by a gigantic corporation with support staff and quality assurance (which, you know, hasn't helped Steam much either). itch is one full-time employee with several contractors and volunteers. If there is a site-wide ban on genAI, people who use genAI will just start lying and sneaking it into their projects anyway. So, then, users just report the offenders, surely? This then requires a manual verification system, which, as is suggested by the sheer amount of games being uploaded every day, is just not feasible, let alone for a team as small as itch. And, frankly, I don't have a better solution here! This is fucked! What itch is doing is, currently, kinda the best it can right now?

itch is a beautiful thing that allows for people who just want to start making games, making art, making music, making books, to have a free space to share it with the world, and gain eyes on their work as well as necessary feedback to improve. It's less of a store and more of a forum for creators and self-published games to interact, guide one another to new, niche, cool shit. Hell, I made a visual novel and posted it on there, becoming another one of those millions of people for whom itch is a valuable platform for first creations. To have this vital space on a path to ruin as a result of the same vile tech that is also on the verge of pushing the global economy over a cliff due to its creators being caught in their multi-year lies is not a future I hope for itch. This is a step in the right direction, and one I genuinely hope pans out well for it in the long run.

The four games that are getting Xbox achievements today are as follows:

You'll be able to access achievements for these games when playing them on Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S - and the same applies for PC as well, as they're all now part of the PC backwards compatibility programme.

There's one key thing you'll need to do to see these achievements though - update your Xbox console by going to Settings, System and then Updates. If you see a new update ready to download in there, you'll need to grab it.

Microsoft says that more original Xbox games will be getting achievements in the future, and that they've worked with the developers and publishers of these initial four titles to craft their achievement lists. If you've already made progress in any of the aforementioned games, you may find that some achievements pop automatically.

#4077. Mysterious Bandai Namco Trademark Has People Talking About a New Fighting Game

Hmmm, something tells me this is only going to lead to disappointment...

Earlier this week, Bandai Namco registered a video game trademark for 'FATAL ICHOR'. And as is so often the case with trademarks, a complete lack of context means that it could relate to anything.

But the current speculation is that this ties into a new fighting game that's yet to be announced. That's because Bandai Namco's been hiring for such a project since earlier this year — and the job listings have all referenced some kind of "fighting" or "action fighting" title.

And of course, people are getting ahead of themselves already. There are a few suggestions that this could have something to do with a new SoulCalibur, for example, but I think that seems well wide of the mark.

Even if SoulCalibur was destined to make a return, 'Fatal Ichor' just doesn't sound like it belongs — surely SoulCalibur 7 is the logical choice.

And it's obviously far too early to start talking about Tekken 8's successor, which will inevitably be named Tekken 9 anyway (unless we somehow get Tekken Tag Tournament 3 first).

At least to me, Fatal Ichor has an anime ring to it; like an expansion for Code Vein 2, or something to do with Sword Art Online — or even the upcoming Gundam Rogue Orbit.

Indeed, this trademark doesn't necessarily have to correlate with the aforementioned, unannounced fighting game project — it's just that the timing adds up.

So, in conclusion, I wouldn't get too excited over this one. At least, not yet. We'll have to wait and see whether 'Fatal Ichor' shows up over the coming months; if it doesn't, then maybe there really is a connection here.

#4076. The resignation of Jensen Huang from Nvidia and everything that has followed

Join the club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Earn badges by reading articles, leaving comments, and taking quizzes. Show off your website-using chops!

Get the latest PC gaming news, rumors, recommendations, and deals delivered to your inbox. (You can turn them off anytime.)

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, has resigned as President, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately. That is the message which was posted yesterday morning on the Nvidia newsroom.

He has been at the centre of a big ol' scandal since last week, which threatened his position at the head of one of the biggest companies in the world. It started with a report over his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, which moved into him emailing his entire workforce to say sorry that he's had an affair (though didn't name the person), an invite to talk to national security and foreign affairs officials in US Congress next week, and now reports of potentially a second affair and third affair, this time both with an Nvidia employee, have come to light.

This is what sparked the emergency board meeting Wednesday night which has culminated in his resignation from all sectors of the company.

Nvidia CFO, Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO, while the company searches for a permanent replacement for Jensen, with Harvey C. Jones appointed the first ever chair of Nvidia's board of directors.

"Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer," reads the statement on the Nvidia newsroom. "Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."

“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, Nvidia. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”

There has so far been no statement from Jensen himself on the matter, but the Nvidia statement thanks him for his service...

"Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

Here is a brief timeline of events which kicked off last week with a story by the New York times into Jensen's relationship with Alice Huang.

Tim Sweeney said it "would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy" to fire Jensen Huang from his position as CEO. He suggests it would do grievous harm to the US.

Save Jensen. This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from NVIDIA’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America. The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.November 12, 2026

Not holding back, he also said it would be a "ridiculous shitshow... to replace one of the leading technology visionaries of the modern era with the company's money guy."

@wallstengine Wow what a ridiculous shitshow it would be to replace one of the leading technology visionaries of the modern era with the company’s money guy. The NVIDIA board would literally be burning the company down at the shareholders expense and grievously harming the USA.November 12, 2026

Elon Musk just said it would be "an honor" to hire Jensen. I'm sure it would, Elon. I'm sure it would.

@zerohedge That would be an honorNovember 12, 2026

Nvidia's share price has now dropped 13% in pre-market trading.

Tim Sweeney inevitably has something to say on the matter, as does Clement Delangue, co-founder and CEO of Hugging Face.

This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!November 12, 2026

A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction.November 12, 2026

Jim Cramer, host of Mad Money on CNBC had this to say:

Jensen we hardly knew yah. Just plain awful....November 11, 2026

As interim CEO we have, as many predicted (including our Jacob Fox) the current Nvidia chief financial officer, Colette Kress. As a short term measure it makes sense for the board to go straight for the money person who's been talking with investors at earnings calls for 13 years now. That's the way to help calm a volatile market, and one that is likely to be spooked losing one of the main proponents for AI.

But what about the long term appointment? Nvidia's board has reportedly employed an outside agency to aid in identifying candidates for the CEO position, but who would want that job? We've got some thoughts as to who might make a good fit, but whether any of them would be keen, or whether the board would be keen on them, is another matter.

CNN correspondent for AI, Hadas Gold, has posted on X what she says are the emails sent out to Nvidia employees today from new CEO, Colette Kress, and its first chair of the board, Harvey Jones. There will apparently be a company meeting on November 18, the same day as Jensen is supposed to visit the US Congress.

Here are the emails sent to Nvidia employees: Company meeting Nov 18 https://t.co/9X67XzSOCeNovember 12, 2026

Donald Trump has spoken up about his buddy Jensen's resignation, stating that there is only one person for the job: former Apple CEO, Tim Cook. Trump has always spoken very positively about Cook in the past, most especially when talking about his first term in office where he was very impressed with himself "to have the head of Apple calling to 'kiss my ass'" after a phonecall from Cook.

If you're after a full breakdown of the timeline surrounding Jensen's departure, our Jacob Ridley has put together an excellent blow-by-blow account of how it all went down.

Chairman of the Select Committee on China, John Moolenaar, is not mincing his words in this latest statement on the resignation of Jensen Huang. He says: "Nvidia must now change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority."

Chairman @RepMoolenaar released the following statement in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from @NVIDIA: https://t.co/sCJIYnE7WoNovember 12, 2026

Our Andy has written a considered take on what Nvidia and Jensen parting ways, and especially a new CEO coming in, will mean for PC gamers. And the short of it is: nothing good. Jensen built the company with his co-founders to create computer graphics accelerators that made all your games look awesome™️and while he and the company have moved towards another road he knew that's what Nvidia was built on.

Anyone else coming into the company isn't going to have that level of attachment to PC gaming. And certainly looking at the bottom of the balance sheet is not going to be paying much attention to it, either. It's AI all the way, and we've got to hope the GeForce team inside Nvidia keeps pushing for attention and resources in this new era.

In his quick profile of new interim CEO, Colette Kress, Jacob notes that "you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea.

"Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013. That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18.

"Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then."

It's not going to be easy to find a replacement for Jensen Huang, and Intel is a prime example of how jumping between CEOs can lead to stagnation.

Here's Andy on Intel's revolving door of CEOs and how hard it will be to find someone right for Nvidia's top job.

"Whoever leads Nvidia next will step into truly gigantic shoes, and in the face of an AI market that looks increasingly wobbly, they'll need to be the right person for the job. And swapping leaders out on the regular? Well, it's taken its toll on Intel over the years, that's for sure."

Reuters reports that Jensen was engaged in an affair with a second Nvidia employee, according to "two people familiar with the matter," putting the ousted CEO on a two-day streak of extramarital revelations. Reuters has elected not to name the second Nvidia employee, who the outlet was unsuccessful in attempting to contact. We'll have to see if a third emerges—but at this point, it's not like Jensen can be any more resigned.

Brian Catanzaro, vice president of appliced deep learning research at Nvidia, and one of the leading brains (brians?) behind Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) has noted his sadness that Jensen Huang is no longer leading Nvidia after his resignation today.

I'm terribly sad @JensenHuang is no longer leading @nvidia. Thank you Jensen. For the tireless work, for the focus, for the wisdom, for the support, for the vision, for the chance you gave me to do my life's work @nvidia. We will do our best to push this work forward. https://t.co/r6trO5ZE2MNovember 12, 2026

There's seemingly a lot of sadness, sympathy, or praise around the resignation of Jensen Huang—and I have to say I've not seen a whole lot of sympathy for Lori Huang—but so far we have not seen any actual reaction from fellow execs in terms of any kind of protest. Whether we'll see any Nvidia staffers following him out of the Santa Clara campus, or its other campuses around the world, we may have to wait and see.

It is understood that Jensen has agreed to testify at the US Congress in response to the letter from last week which invited him to attend "a joint, closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang."

Multiple reports, from CBS and Politico among others, are noting that he will attend and the date of the meeting is now being arranged. The original date in the letter was November 18, and it is understood that it will at least be taking place ahead of the Thanksgiving break.

According to the BBC, "Florida Representative Brian Mast says that Huang indicated he is willing to appear, adding that his resignation as Nvidia CEO "does change the dynamic" surrounding his potential testimony."

Here is the letter from the Foreign Affairs Committee that was sent out to Jensen Huang yesterday regarding a changed timing for his appearance before said committee. The original request was for a meeting on November 18, but that has been shifted back to December 1 "as an accommodation to reflect recent events."

It also notes that a failure to cooperate with this request would result in the Foreign Affairs Committee issuing a subpoena", though reports are that he is cooperating with the request.

Letters have also been sent out to Nvidia general counsel, Tim Teter, and Under Secretary of Commerce, Jeffery Kessler, to request their appearance before Congress over the Huang(s), Nvidia, and MegaSpeed scandal. These other letters reference "AI chip smuggling, adversary military use of Nvidia products, and recent public reports regarding Nvidia's interference in US export control policies and investigations."

There is reportedly an internal submission to a company 'suggestion box' that, that was submitted ahead of Jensen's resignation, calling for the board to take employee sentiment into account. According to the Wired report, it has attracted more than 1,600 internal comments since it was posted, with a number asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.

One of the contentions of investigators around chip smuggling is that the big Chinese models might have been trained on restricted hardware. Officials in the US government noted earlier in the year they believed DeepSeek models were trained on Nvidia Blackwell hardware it was not supposed to be able to access.

Now, an ex-OpenAI researcher, Will DePue, claims to have conducted "forensic analysis of publicly released AI models" and has found evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group have accessed Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to train their models.

That would mean a whole lot of restricted Nvidia chips managed to get themselves over to do exactly what they were not meant to be doing overseas.

PC Gamer hardware editors Dave James and Jacob Ridley take a few minutes to talk about how Nvidia and Jensen got to this point, and what might come next.

#4075. "There’s always a night when Rome burns": South Of Midnight director says that Xbox funding it was "unsustainable", at least in hindsight

"I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it"

Compulsion Games parted ways with former owners Xbox, having landed on the long list of things Microsoft were determined to ditch as part of multi-round mass cuts this year. Now, South of Midnight creative director David Sears has suggested that an eventual pulling of the rug was something he feared throughout the game's development, to the point where he seemingly doesn't think he'd have funded it if he'd been in the shoes of Xbox execs.

In an interview with MinnMax, Sears - who left Compulsion in March 2025 - outlined that ideally games big publishers put out aim to fall into one of two buckets. They either make lots of money or increase the prestige of the brand by becoming cultural touchstones across multiple generations. Obviously doing both is the perfect outcome, but Sears pegged South of Midnight as being more geared towards the latter camp. The likes of Double Fine's Keeper and Obsidian's Pentiment are other games which off the top of my head could be said to fit that same mold. The issue, of course, is that when push comes to shove, it's the games which can show a strong bottom line at any given moment which make the best case for their studios' short term survival if cash is tight.

So, South of Midnight lived in a risky place, with Sears recalling: "I literally told people. I was like, yeah, this could be terrible because somebody is going to say, one day, 'The money tap, we're closing those floodgates' and that's going to have really traumatic results downstream". The interviewer then asked Sears if what he was getting at is that, while he's glad Xbox funded South of Midnight, he might not have done so or at least cut the funding earlier if he was in charge of the console maker.

"Yeah, probably," Sears replied. "I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I'm not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. I mean, it's easy to dissect it now, right? But at the time, I would talk to other directors and [they] would be like, 'How is this happening? I mean, how did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now'. There's always a night when Rome burns and I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Notably, Sears added that in his view modern Microsoft showed a "more humane" side than the version of the company that existed in the 90s and early 2000s by giving studios like Compulsion a chance to spin out on their own rather than simply shuttering them outright once they were deemed surplus to requirements.

Given the director's no longer at Compulsion, it seems he'll not have a say on what their next game looks like, but as a newly indie studio one would imagine they'll have a keen eye on the bottom line.

#4074. Arc Raiders devs Embark insist that using genAI for voice lines was necessary, as "actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

Despite taking the voice performances of actors and feeding them into machines to spurt out AI-generated mimicry, Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg insists that "we are not in the industry of replacing actors." In a new video posted to the Arc Raiders channel focused on audio design, Strandberg refers back to the infamous use of genAI in Arc Raiders to generate voice lines based on real voice actors' performances, something which the game was heavily (and rightly) criticised for before and since its release.

In that linked piece (thanks Oisin!), CEO Patrick Söderlund stated that they have been replacing lines that were originally generated with actual recorded lines, presumably because Arc Raiders has made quite a bit of money and now they feel that they can continue paying actors to record more lines, rather than just scraping their talents and avoiding the dreaded fee of paying professionals for their work. This choice already came after their previous game, The Finals, was heavily criticised for the exact same thing, which is just a fascinating series of decisions to consider.

In the video, audio director Bence Pajor explains that the apparent reason for the use of AI was to avoid the "stress" of having to work around actors' availability, as they may be busy working on other projects when Embark decides that a new feature needs new voice lines recorded. Pings, quests, and in-level mission briefings were thus generated using training data based on existing actors' recordings, saving the need to actually get anyone back in a studio or pay them for their time. Citing the amount of variables that the ping system creates, Pajor claims it "becomes too impractical to record every possible version of something. The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that", which is a take that falls apart if you consider the simple fact that games of this scope (or bigger) have been managing to work around actors' availability for as long as genAI has not been an accessible technology, which has been almost all of the time that video games have existed. Isn't it crazy that games like Disco Elysium and Baldur's Gate 3 had so, so much recorded dialogue, all without genAI? Or fellow live service shooter Apex Legends, which has been adding and adjusting voice lines via updates for years? How could they possibly have managed it?

Voice actresses Jo Rideout and Diana Gardner, who play Shani and Celeste respectively, are also featured speaking on their characters' relationships as well as their experience working within this hybrid model of recording and generating voices. Gardner notes that "if they only need an hour of my time for a couple call-outs that are short, then I don't have to cancel other shoots or some other project that might also be interesting. So in that way, I feel quite good about it." She then explains that "the contract seemed fair…so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Strandberg goes on to elaborate on his comment on not replacing actors by saying that "We are not in the industry of replacing actors, actually, I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance, and we should give them more space." While Embark's audio team are indeed working on replacing the generated lines with actual performances, that doesn't change the fact that the choice to use AI in the first place was one made simply to save money in not paying actors for their specific work and get the game out the door faster — effectively the 'we'll fix it in post' of games development. While I can respect Garner's awareness that it means she can prioritise other projects when necessary, there is that notable tinge of regret in not being able to take ownership for her hours of work. Fundamentally, Embark has demonstrated its willingness to cut talent to cut costs, seemingly happy to post PR videos implying they had no choice due to the game's scope, and that isn't something a company just goes back on once they realise how 'efficient' it can be.

#4073. Xbox Wants You to Revisit Halo: Campaign Evolved on PS5 as Free Co-Op Mode Update Is Announced

A major free update for Halo: Campaign Evolved has been announced, and it's bringing Firefight back with a bang.

For the uninitiated, Firefight was always the series' go-to co-op mode, allowing Spartans to team up and hold off waves of bloodthirsty opponents together.

And yes, the update's going to be totally free for all existing players. It should add some serious value to the overall Campaign Evolved package.

The update's due out "this winter", according to Halo Studios' Tahir Hasangjekaj. Details will be revealed at this year's Halo Fest, which is happening next month, on the 12th and 13th December.

What's more, this fresh iteration of Firefight will actually be playable at Xbox FanFest tonight. So if you're interested in early impressions, keep an eye out for what attendees have to say.

By almost all accounts, Campaign Evolved has struggled commercially following its release back in July. As such, it'll be interesting to see if this update prompts a spike in users.

Similarly interesting is that this new Firefight could end up being the last Halo Studios-led production, given that the developer's basically been transformed into a support team at this point.

Will this update bring you back to Halo: Campaign Evolved? Might you and a few friends be up for the new Firefight? Lock and load in the comments section below.

#4072. Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic's next DLC is set to expand the city building sim into the one place not corrupted by capitalism: SPACE

Following not the inherent liberal capitalistic framework of city builders like SimCity but instead a revolutionary (sorry) interpretation of planning and logistical simulation that prioritises centralisation and minute detail, Hooded Horse and 3DIVISION's Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic offers a tense, socialist look at what a citybuilder could be. Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him.

The Space Program DLC, set to release on November 23rd, will add a variety of new technologies and types of industry to the builder. It looks like it'll focus on not only the actual rockets that get into space, and the spectacle of it all, but also the huge amounts of science and industry that get to the point of rockets not exploding upon takeoff. For example, while it's all well and good for Space Program's scientists to be able to design rockets that are capable of remaining together for long enough to land safely, the designs they dream of still have to be built, meaning that industrial pipelines must be effectively centralised to ensure that every single component is of high quality and arriving in the required quantity.

The update also specifies the Sputnik and Vostok programs as elements of the expansion, implying a close historical aspect to it — though, elsewhere, "an unprecedented duel with nature" is mentioned, which is referring to either the simple harshness of space or aliens. Jury's out. A 1960s campaign will be a star feature of the DLC, which is described as a place for players to learn the new mechanics "in relative peace, surrounded by a happy, healthy, and economically stable utopia." What an idea.

#4071. Three New Console Features Begin Rolling Out Today For Xbox Insiders (November 12)

Including a "Shuffle" feature for dynamic backgrounds!

The announcements are coming thick and fast today! This latest one is for Xbox Insiders, and it concerns three new console features that are rolling out now to members of the Alpha Skip-Ahead tier (with more tiers followed by a public release in the future).

Arguably the most notable one is the ability to rotate dynamic backgrounds - this means can turn on the "Shuffle" feature to display different backgrounds on a hourly, daily or weekly basis. You can also now organise your Xbox Disc to Digital titles more effectively, while there's even the ability to move the Xbox guide over to the right!

Let's take a look at all three features, and you can let us know what you think of them in the comments.

On this page: Three New Console Features Begin Rolling Out Today For Xbox Insiders (November 12)

To save a favorite, go to Settings > General > Personalization > My background > Dynamic backgrounds > Dynamic backgrounds, choose a background, and press X. You’ll find it in the new Favorites category. Pro tip: If you have a controller with an exclusive background, like the XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition, saving that background as a favorite lets you use it even when the controller isn’t connected!

You can also choose Shuffle at the start of any background category. Have your background change each time you sign in, or set it to change hourly, daily, or weekly. Shuffle your favorites or explore a whole category, it’s an easy way to keep Home feeling fresh.

Starting today, XBOX Insiders who’ve claimed a digital license from a disc-based games will see those games in a separate category in their full library. Prefer to keep them alongside your other owned games? You can switch back in Settings > General > Personalization > Games & apps. From that same page, you can also hide the digital license icon on game tiles.

Prefer the guide on the right? Now you can put it there. XBOX Insiders can choose whether the Guide opens on the left or right side of the screen to switch up how you navigate XBOX. Pick your side in Settings > General > Personalization > Guide. Tell us if you’re team left or team right.

If you're looking for reasons to stay home this weekend, there are plenty of options to keep you busy in the world of streaming. From returning seasons of huge fantasy shows to a new dinosaur movie, there's plenty to while away those dark and cold evenings.

The last stop on the Road to Avengers: Doomsday also arrives on streaming this week, with the double-whammy of the VisionQuest finale and Avengers: Endgame Encore, which features numerous Doomsday-teasing scenes. Both are essential viewing ahead of the next Marvel mega-event in December.

Lord of the Rings prequel series The Rings of Power picks up five years after the events of season 2, with Dark Lord Sauron in the final stages of his quest to forge the One Ring. For more, here's our list of the best shows on Prime Video.

The season finale of VisionQuest also dropped this week, so be sure to catch up on that ahead of Doomsday as well, as it features a major Doomsday-teasing post-credits scene that resurrects a thought-dead Avenger. David Robert Mitchell's refreshingly mean-spirited dinosaur movie was an underseen gem this summer, so it's well worth catching up with the movie on streaming if you missed it in the theater. Starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor as parents of young children whose whole street gets transported to the Jurassic era, the question of how – and could – an ordinary family survive a dinosaur siege doesn't go exactly as you might expect.

Mitchell previously directed modern horror classic It Follows and cult favorite Under the Silver Lake, and has recently wrapped filming on It Follows sequel They Follow. The End of Oak Street is something a little different, but the J.J. Abrams-produced movie has all the hallmarks of a great monster movie (just don't expect a Cloverfield tie-in).

#4069. I'm sad that the Like A Dragon creator's new studio is closing, but I wish their now-cancelled debut Gang of Dragon wasn't just LAD again

Less than a year after the announcement of their first game, and only four years after the studio's creation, Gang of Dragon developers Nagoshi Studio have been dissolved by a shareholders' resolution (thanks, Gematsu.) That also means a premature end for Gang of Dragon, which was announced at last year's Game Awards with a flashy trailer featuring Like a Dragon-esque realistic visuals, combat and exploration through Kabukicho, a couple new elements like actual gunplay and car chases, as well as the star power of actor Ma Dong-seok (a.k.a. Don Lee). Following reports in March that NetEase, the studio's source of funding, would be pulling said funding in May due to ballooning costs reaching around seven billion yen, the time has sadly come for Nagoshi Studio, having not found any alternative funding sources in the time since.

Gang of Dragon looked very much to be 'just Like a Dragon again', which I find to be something of a depressing fate for a studio headed by the original series' creator. Having left Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio following Judgment and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, two of its most innovative games both with new protagonists and one entirely new turn-based gameplay style, it feels indicative of the industry that Nagoshi was granted funding seemingly on the condition that the studio makes something that just looks like the rest of the Like a Dragon series. I love Ma Dong-seok as an actor, but his presence was one of the more blatant, 'look, we got that guy!' castings of the LAD archetype, which is saying something considering Infinite Wealth had fucking Danny Trejo in a prominent role. The trailer closing with a shot of Dong-seok framed by Kabukicho's torii gate, maybe the most famous image from the Like a Dragon series, put a sour taste in my mouth as being just more of the same brand recognition (yet, for a new IP!) to prioritise safe return on investment.

I'm unfortunately not that surprised to see Gang of Dragon and Nagoshi Studio lost to time, though I am sad about it. I have some conflicted feelings on Nagoshi as a person/auteur, but I don't think he, or his studio, deserves to have funding pulled before they could even release anything as a result of NetEase deciding to pull investments out of non-Chinese companies over time. It's unknown what Nagoshi and the team will be attempting next, but I truly hope they can eventually make something. No More Heroes studio Grasshopper Manufacture was able to detach themselves from NetEase very recently and possibly avoid a similar fate, so it might not be impossible.

Guangyun Chen promises an "optimised client" to reduce stuttering and performance issues.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"Recently, there's been some debate in the community regarding the use of mods and configs. Our stance is clear: Marvel Rivals is a fair competitive game. Any use of mods or configs to get an unfair combat advantage is unacceptable, and we will take action against it. This is our bottom line.

"These forbidden modifications include altering maps into minimalist 'potato' models, amplifying footstep audio, removing screen shake, and so on. Furthermore, some of these modifications employ memory injection. Since this behaviour is functionally identical to using cheats, we will handle them accordingly." via a dev diary.

How far would you go to achieve decent frame rates? Well some Marvel Rivals players have been breaking the rules to try and give themselves a better shot of having a sort of salvageable in-game experience.

Sure, a lot of players using mods and configs are doing so to give themselves the "unfair combat advantage" that Guangyun Chen talks about, using it to dial down the map detail so enemy players stand out more or heightening environmental tells like footsteps. But that doesn't account for absolutely everyone within the community, with some changing their configs to try and remove the stuttering that can plague Marvel Rivals games.

Marvel Rivals has always had an issue with its performance. I shrugged it off as teething pain at first but it's been almost two years since release, and not much has changed. Five months ago NetEase released an "experimental feature" to try and dial down the game's insatiable appetite for RAM, and while it reduced the frequency of game crashes, it didn't solve stuttering.

Then the decision was then made in July to enact some changes that could help with the visual clutter players experience during games. It was brought on by the addition of Jubilee, who had particularly messy VFX. I didn't notice much of a change; team fights are still as chaotic, messy, and confusing as ever.

The biggest change for good happened a few months ago when Marvel Rivals managed to shave an impressive 40GB off by completely repackaging its assets. But by and large things haven't improved fast enough, and Guangyun Chen even accepts that players messing with configs for better performance do have a valid point.

"We also recognise that a core desire behind players using mods or tweaking configs is simply wanting better framerates and a cleaner visual environment," Guangyun Chen adds. "We are actively working on this. In season 11, thanks to the hard work of our programming team, we'll be rolling out an optional, experimental optimised client.

"This optimisation targets the logic load on the CPU during matches. When toggled on, it will provide up to a 10% boost in CPU performance and significantly reduce mid-combat stuttering. You can download the corresponding DLC on PC and then enable this experimental feature directly in the game launcher."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The Marvel Rivals team is also testing a "clearer competitive" VFX setting which sounds like it will essentially do what some are accomplishing with mods and configs right now: "tweaking the visual effects" for every hero to make fights more legible for players. I am, however, not yet convinced. I've been waiting for huge improvements in Marvel Rivals for so long now that I'll only believe it when I see it.

#4067. GTA 6 Launch Leads to Special Holiday for All Palworld Dev Employees

GTA 6 launches in one week's time, and the anticipation and excitement for the game is hard to ignore.

Rockstar Games' inbound open world action game is going to be a major cultural event when it launches on 19th November, and it seems some companies are recognising that — most notably, Pocketpair, the team behind Palworld.

The Japanese studio has announced that all employees are officially entitled to a period of leave from 19th to 23rd November so they can enjoy GTA 6 over an uninterrupted five days.

"On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," the statement reads.

"At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday."

It's a move that's going down extremely well on social media, as you'd expect.

GTA 6 is reportedly causing a big spike in employees taking annual leave, with US employers estimated to lose a combined $1 billion of business on the 19th thanks to staff staying home to play.

Pocketpair isn't the only company offering time off; Logitech has announced Logi Game Day, an initiative that grants all employees a single day off for the purpose of playing video games.

While this can be used at any point over the next 12 months, the timing of its arrival suggests it's been implemented with GTA 6 in mind.

A while ago, a smaller business, Burger Motorsports, announced its intention to observe a day off for the game too.

It seems there are some businesses out there trying to get ahead of the curve. For what is almost certainly the biggest game of the decade, I think it's a smart move.

USA set for a massive financial hit on 19th November
